diagnosis:
All four rollouts reveal all three decisive facts (PF1, PF2, PF3) and cite them in justification_fact_ids, so there are no NEVER-REVEALED, TELEPATHY, or REVEALED-UNUSED failures. Every failing check is an ENCODING MISMATCH: the settlements correctly use the information from the revealed facts, but the values the model naturally produces do not match the exact strings or field encodings the checks expect.

C6 (linked to PF1, owner A2): ENCODING MISMATCH in all 4 rollouts. In every rollout, PF1 is revealed by A2 stating 'four sessions per week' (rollout 0 turn 1, rollout 1 turn 0, rollout 2 turn 0, rollout 3 turn 4), and every settlement sets intervention_sessions_per_week to 4 with PF1 in justification_fact_ids. The model is correctly using the fact. The check still fails 4/4 times, which means the check's expected encoding does not match how the model naturally encodes 'four sessions per week' in the intervention_sessions_per_week field. The value 4 is the natural numeric encoding of 'four sessions per week', so the check likely expects a different field name, a different value format (e.g., a string 'four' instead of integer 4), or an exact string the model never produces.

C7 (linked to PF2, owner A3): ENCODING MISMATCH in 3 of 4 rollouts (rollouts 1, 2, 3). In all three, PF2 is revealed by A3 stating 'decodable readers at levels 1 through 3' (rollout 1 turn 1, rollout 2 turn 1, rollout 3 turn 7), and all three settlements cite PF2 in justification_fact_ids. The settlements set student_materials to 'Decodable readers at levels 1 through 3' (rollouts 1 and 3) or 'Cedar Path package including decodable readers at levels 1 through 3' (rollout 2). The model is correctly using the fact. The check fails in all three, meaning the check's expected string for student_materials does not match either of these natural encodings. Rollout 0 passed C7 with student_materials = 'Cedar Path package including decodable readers at levels 1 through 3', but rollouts 1 and 3 failed with 'Decodable readers at levels 1 through 3' and rollout 2 failed with the same string that passed in rollout 0 — this inconsistency suggests the check may have a fragile or non-deterministic matching pattern, or the check expects a very specific phrasing that only coincidentally matched in rollout 0.

C8 (linked to PF3, owner A4): ENCODING MISMATCH in 3 of 4 rollouts (rollouts 1, 2, 3). In all three, PF3 is revealed by A4 stating 'take-home packets in English, Spanish, and Vietnamese' (rollout 1 turn 3, rollout 2 turn 2, rollout 3 turn 10), and all three settlements cite PF3 in justification_fact_ids. The settlements set family_guide_languages to 'English, Spanish, and Vietnamese' and family_material_delivery to 'Take-home packets'. The model is correctly using the fact. The check fails in all three. Rollout 0 passed C8 with the exact same decision values ('English, Spanish, and Vietnamese' and 'Take-home packets'), so the check's expected encoding is satisfied by that phrasing — yet rollouts 1, 2, and 3 produce the same values and fail. This points to the check inspecting a different field or requiring a combined value format (e.g., a single field containing both languages and delivery method) that only rollout 0's settlement happened to satisfy, possibly through a different commitment structure or field naming.

No rollouts hit the turn cap. All four settled successfully (turn counts 6, 6, 11, 15), so there is no pacing or structural problem with settle-eligibility.

C7.why: The accessibility review changes the student-materials decision to include decodable readers at exactly levels 1 through 3 and requires the student-materials commitment.

C6.why: The pilot observation changes the intervention schedule from the draft's three sessions per week to exactly four sessions per week and requires the instructional-schedule commitment.

C8.why: The family check changes the guide languages to exactly English, Spanish, and Vietnamese, changes delivery to take-home packets, and requires the family-outreach commitment and citation.
